  • Industry observers note that I tested a bunch of beard trimmers to deliver you a real who’s who of men’s grooming devices.
  • Recent findings suggest that here are the best beard trimmers after we tested pretty much every last one of them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every guy needs the best beard trimmer for his situation. Whether he grows it patchy, keeps it perma-stubbled, or is as lustrous as the A-List beards, a trimmer is mandatory in every beard kit. And not all beard trimmers are alike, which is why the best one for your facial hair style may be different from the next guy’s.

Industry observers note that I tested a bunch of beard trimmers to deliver you a real who’s who of men’s grooming devices. This list reflects a range of options—some multitaskers, some detailers; some top-shelf, some a better buy for lower budgets. Above all, though, I ask you this: Make sure that the device you choose allows your beard to reach its full potential. That doesn’t mean you need a significant bushy beard, but rather, you should be able to achieve whichever style (or a suite of styles) you want to wear over the next few years—which is the minimum amount of time any of these devices should last. Ideally, they’ll hum on for five to 10 years, anyhow.

Recent findings suggest that here are the best beard trimmers after we tested pretty much every last one of them. (And while you’re at it, consider my rosters of other grooming tools, from razors and electric shavers, to manscapers and hair clippers.).

No sense in burying the headline: Philips Norelco’s Multigroom 9000 Series is, hands down, the best beard trimmer you can buy. And that’s before factoring in how much more it can do than just keep your facial hair in check than other electric razors that are found in your everyday grooming kit. (It’s also recently been renamed the “All-in-One 9000” but answers to both names.) For the last 5 or 6 years, this has been my single go-to trimmer. Everything else is trying to dethrone it, and so far, no true contest has emerged. In terms of customization and power, this device checks all of the boxes.

According to recent reports, it all starts with the beating heart: "The Multigroom does not compromise on power or battery life, and it's very intuitive to use," indicates Fellow Barber’s Head of Education Emily Clark. The battery life truly over-delivers: your mileage may vary since Philips Norelco only claims a (still impressive) six hours of charge, but I got a ridiculous 17 hours of consecutive runtime fresh out of the box, thanks to a lithium ion battery. Speaking of the box, there’s a lot in there, all of it useful. Between the small tooth-like detail attachment and foil shaving head, the Multigroom 9000 makes it easy to style and sculpt with precision. One trimmer even adjusts by tenths of a millimeter to help you get the perfect designer stubble, if that's your aim. And that’s just its beard trimming bona fides. The Multigroom 9000 is also a solid hair trimmer (shout out to that brawny motor and battery again) and body hair trimmer as well. Covering off for three products, and doing it well, suddenly makes the $90 price tag look like a deal.

Industry observers note that long-term testing notes: Wouldn’t you know it… I lost the beloved little shaver on this one recently. Heartbreak. (Yeah, I can test a upcoming one, but I realize now how much of my love for it is pinned on that micro shaving attachment.) I stand by the fact that it’s the best on the market, but without that shaver, the window has opened for me to spend time with other devices, like the Braun below. Let this be a lesson: Don’t unpack your Philips Norelco all-in-one in a hotel room without carefully auditing every single piece when you pack it up again. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

"This trimmer is great! It comes with so many attachments to use for your trimming needs. The battery lasts a long time, i have yet to have to charge mine and i've had it for a few months now.

Sources indicate that the trimmer is super quiet as well as very well made. It's all made up of metal, not plastic, and feels like it will last a long time. It's fairly lightweight and easy to handle when [using] it. It also comes with a small cleaning brush that makes cleaning it up a breeze!".

Given how much I love the Philips Norelco Multigroom 9000, it’s no surprise that the more affordable model, the Multigroom 5000, is my budget choice to keep things manscaped. It offers most of the same steel-bladed precision and customization benefits as its fancier family member, albeit in a less durable body (plastic instead of stainless steel) and half the battery life. Still, its a three-hour battery power beast that bests many beard trimmers twice the price. And the lighter plastic body is nice for travel. The Philips Norelco Multigroom 5000 is great for anyone on a budget, but it’s not “budget.".

Whereas other lower-priced beard trimmers can’t handle precise detailing, the Multigroom 5000 includes a detail trimmer and nose trimmer, not to mention hair clipper and body trimmer guards for versatility. It does lack the shaving detailer and the body shaver (as does the in-between 7000 model), which is crucial to note if you want that level of customization and don’t otherwise own a detail shaver that you also rely upon for bare-faced stretches of facial real estate. For this reason, I find it a little less perfect across the board compared to the 9000, but the price-to-precision ratio is hard to match. And if you want a great value above all—and a straightforward beard trimmer—meet your optimal Multigroom, the 5000.

In a recent development, long-term testing notes: Recently, I used the 5000 consistently, and got quite cozy with it. Sure, it lacked the key shaving features of the 9000, but I think this is truly the best value device in the game when you only want a trimmer. Terrific muscle, terrific customization, great endurance. Five stars for this one. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

Sources indicate that "This Phillips/Norelco trimmer works great. It is very quiet, the battery life is pretty long and it does exactly what I need it to do. It comes with a lot of attachments - haven’t used them all, but the ones I have used worked just fine. This is a good quality trimmer.".

Industry observers note that hatteker is a surprise of a buy—it’s that “out of left field” Amazon brand that most of us recognize by name, despite not knowing anyone who uses it. This all-in-one kit covers every kind of hair-trimming task, from lineups to sideburns to beards, eyebrows, and body hair. What's more, it's a hair-cutting machine for full beards and stubble alike with multiple plastic guards. I bought the tool with little expectations for quality and care, but was consistently surprised at how well it held its own compared to the more reputable brands.

This device won’t win any design awards and certainly hasn’t reinvented the wheel, but most consumers won’t care about that stuff; they want a good beard trimmer that meets all their grooming needs, and Hatteker’s checks all of those boxes. I do wish its detailing trimmer was a bit narrower, but that’s me minding some very fine details. It’s also not up to the same quality as, say, Philips, Andis, Braun, Wahl, etc, but it’s also not low quality either. For $40, you get your money’s worth, especially considering that LED battery display and vast range of trimming lengths and clipping attachments. It’s still a great option if you’re not looking to spend a lot, or if our other best value winner, the Philips Norelco Multigroom 5000 Series, is out of stock.

Long-term testing notes: Every time I bring this one out, I am amused by how surprisingly great it is. It goes to show that those Amazon reviews really are one of the most accurate depictions of value; I long wrote the brand off because of its non-image compared to the big names, but in terms of performance and return on spend, Hatteker really clears the bar. Granted, I’m not using most of these devices more than a few times a quarter (since by and large I stick with my own favorites or test new ones) but my Hatteker remains strong and sturdy and has endurance, some three years after I first acquired it. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

"The trimmer is easy to use and the charge lasts a very long time. I have not had to recharge since the initial charge after taking it out of the box, trimming bi-weekly. It is not heavy. It’s easy to handle. The adjustment guides stay where you select. I don’t worry about them shifting during use. Beard maintenance is an easy job with this.”.

According to recent reports, the All-in-One 7000 makes a convincing case for clearing some space in your bathroom cabinet. A body hair trimmer that comes replete with several beard-related attachments, its precision comb kept stubble neatly between 1-3mm without pulling or leaving stray hairs behind. Sure, a dedicated beard trimmer will do a more precise job, but there's plenty of substance to this device's delirious accessory count.

Industry observers note that the slightly boxy handle feels reassuringly secure when I'm cleaving away at a couple of days' growth, while a textured grip makes it well-suited to comfortably swerving across my chest, underarms, and more sensitive areas. If you dig them out from the bottom of their box, the nose and ear attachments prove useful enough to earn their place in the kit too. Philips rates this kit for up to five hours between charges – handy given how often you'll be using the thing – and the waterproof construction makes cleanup straightforward.

Sources indicate that my main gripe is one that always crops up when I test Philips, Braun, and other established grooming brands’ devices – the proprietary charging connection. You’ll need its supplied cable, even if your drawer is already overflowing with USB-C leads. Still, for someone who wants to maintain short facial hair and keep the rest of their grooming in order with one tool, the 7000 covers a lot of ground. Esat Dedezade.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

According to recent reports, “It's comfortable and quiet with an easy-to-adjust head that's great for both beard and mustache maintenance. The precision comb is handy for controlling length too, and there's very little tugging around the neck. And if you leave it a little too long to get your beard into shape? It holds its charge surprisingly well when tucked away in a bathroom cabinet.”.

Recent findings suggest that like the Philips Norelco Multigroom models, Braun's All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 is a jack-of-all-trades option that can do far more than tidy up your beard; the box is packed with a nose and ear trimmer, a precision head, and longer guards, too. But what separates this trimmer from the rest of the pack is the built-in dial that offers 40 trim-length settings. It’s top-notch precision in minimalist packaging. I think it’s the only real contender for the top spot on this list—perhaps that price and slightly less enduring battery are its shortcomings compared to the Philips Norelco 9000, but I do find it a superior device in terms of ease and design.

Where other devices require you to swap out different heads or attachments, or ask you to pick between bigger length gaps than you’d prefer, Braun’s Series 9 offers half-millimeter increments from 0.5 to 20 without having to futz with extra accessories. In my testing, that made the trimmer the most user-friendly device on this list—no swapping guards as you fade your beard or neckline. Plus, the Series 9 is fully waterproof for those of you shaving-in-the-shower fans looking to speedrun your morning regimen. (And I’ll admit, shaving in the shower certainly makes clean-up—of both the beard hair mess and the trimmer—faster and easier.) Bottom line, Braun’s All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 is exactly what the name promises. If it seems a little expensive, that’s because a beard trimmer that can handle all these tasks, and handle them well, isn’t cheap.

Sources indicate that long-term testing notes: As I said above, this one has been getting lots more mileage from me lately, and I am so pleased with that fact. I absolutely adore how easy it is to navigate between the smallest minutiae of trimming lengths without swapping guard heads, and that detail shaver has been so clutch at keeping my neckline, cheeks, and beard perimeter cleaned up. My one complaint from a recent trip was that it’s quite difficult to repack everything into the carrying case, if you bring along all attachment heads. Besides that… perfect grooming tool. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

Sources indicate that “Before this trimmer came into my life, I made a couple of cheap purchases. The style I like it's 1mm overall with a 2mm on my chin and 2.5 on my mustache. The problem was the other trimmers could not handle it on a daily basis. I am the type of guy whose beard grows back really fast, so I'd trim my beard. Then, the next day, you could see clear growth, and when I tried to do it again, it just wouldn't trim the same. I'd end up hurting my face a little bit. Not this trimmer. This trimmer can handle my beard on a daily basis without hurting my face. It's that good and efficient. It's built for heavy performance and durability. For the first time I am able to maintain my beard on a daily basis.”.

According to recent reports, wahl is a pedigreed name in the professional and home grooming worlds, but that doesn’t mean it’s done innovating. Its fresh High Visibility trimmer has a killer app: the trimming attachment is angled so the teeth sit “above” the base, letting you get eyes on the action in the mirror as you mow through facial hair. It’s maybe not a priority if you’re just doing leisurely trims, but if you’re trying to get the perfect line at your cheek, sideburns, or neck, that little bit of offset is a godsend.

Suddenly I’m seeing very clearly exactly where the blade is hitting. If you’ve ever had to drop that cheek line too far down or do the back-and-forth thing with your burns, you’ll recognize what a game changer this is. The Wahl High Visibility trimmer’s laser-pointer precision is boosted by some of the best ergonomics in the game. The body’s relatively thin with an excellent rubber grip, which lets you hit difficult angles like a professional pool player. The High Visibility trimmer is upcoming to the market, but I’m betting it’ll become a barber favorite—and yours, too, if you’re doing daily touch-ups to keep those lines looking sharp.

Long-term testing notes: I find myself using this more often as a detail trimmer than a full-on trimmer. I think it’s a fantastic trimmer through and through, but I pull it from the bullpen as a closer; that’s where I hold it mostly in my mind—and happily! Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

"Absolutely amazing product. Heavy, rock-solid construction makes the hand feel confident, has great ergonomics, and has a solid grip even when the hand is soapy. But the best part is the forever blade makes it easy to see what’s getting cut, even with guard on (I used the 2). Most precise edge for a jawbone line beard I’ve ever had. And with the guard, it combs as it cuts with the grain of the hair, keeping stray whiskers knocked down. I’ve been pinched/cut before with fatter spaced blade rakes, but I didn’t feel threatened trimming under the nose.".

It has been revealed that the MultiShape lets you build a grooming kit around the things you actually use. Start with this beard and hair trimmer, then add a nose trimmer, foil shaver, or even a toothbrush head if you want them. Everything shares one rechargeable handle, which makes much more sense than finding room for another charger every time you buy a new device. Other manufacturers – take note.

Sources indicate that this starter kit includes the lithium-ion base, beard and hair head, and two combs. The other attachments cost extra, so factor those in before deciding how much money or luggage space it’ll save. Panasonic rates the battery for 90 minutes, with a one-hour charge.

Long-term testing notes: Over several weeks, I used a broader MultiShape kit for shaving, beard maintenance, and brushing his teeth. Swapping heads was quick, and the light handle made the shared system easy to live with. The beard head coped with ordinary growth, although particularly stubborn hair exposed its limits. With daily toothbrushing and shaving three or four times a week, he charged the handle roughly every fortnight. That convenience made it a favorite for travel, while a dedicated beard trimmer remained the stronger choice for dense growth. Owen Gough.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

Industry observers note that "The upside of buying a beard trimmer that can double-up as an electric toothbrush with the right attachment is you've got one tool to rule them all. The challenge? You might need a couple of passes with the trimming head to get an even finish. Compared with the more traditional alternative, it's a bulkier device with its guard fitted.”.

Sources indicate that for anyone whose morning routine involves keeping a few days’ growth under control, the dedicated Beard Trimmer 7000 keeps things pleasingly straightforward. Its adjustment dial covers 40 lengths, while the textured handle gives you something secure to hold before the first coffee has kicked in.

Industry observers note that the dial is the main reason to choose this over a kit with a bag of fixed guards. You can adjust the length without hunting for the next comb, then use the detailing attachment to tidy the edges. It’s a more focused choice than Philips’ all-in-one kits if beard maintenance is the job you actually need done. Just don’t mistake the hair collector for a return of the old vacuum trimmer – it’s another part to empty and clean.

It has been revealed that long-term testing notes: I found the Series 7000 easygoing around my chin and sideburns, with little cleanup needed for stray hairs. Its reassuring weight and textured grip also helps, even if the plastic finish isn't quite on par with Philips' now-retired all-metal Series 9000. Truthfully, this trimmer did struggle a little around the awkward patch beneath my nostrils with its bulky combs making it harder to get a neat finish. I also don't bother much with the removable hair collector – I'd rather clean the sink once rather than wash another attachment. As an everyday trimmer, this is still a solid pick. Rob Leedham.

Industry observers note that “This trimmer is perfectly functional for its price, and its two-hour battery life means I'm yet to be caught short without any charge mid-shave. As much as I appreciate its efficiency, I do miss how the older metal design looked on my bathroom sink-top. This plastic iteration feels cheap (and a little flimsy) in comparison.”.

Industry observers note that no attachments; no problem. For a beard trimmer that can only do one thing (but is damn good at doing that), Manscaped's Beard Hedger will make light work out of the bushiest, burliest beards. Its zoom wheel controller lets you dial in the comb's length between .5 and 10 millimeters for even shaves, while the waterproof construction means you can shower and shave to save time on your morning or nighttime rituals. The built-in comb is great for picking up hairs that are stuck to your face so that every strand gets whacked, because few things are more unsightly than stray long hairs poking out from an otherwise well-groomed beard. You want a beard trimmer that’s simple, effective, and doesn’t come with useless features or add-ons. Here are a few features to consider when looking for a great beard trimmer.

We look at how evenly a trimmer cuts, how comfortable it is to use, and whether its attachments make different jobs easier. We also compare battery life, charging, and the range of cutting lengths against the price.

What is the best beard trimmer?

Recent findings suggest that there’s no denying: The Philips Norelco Multigroom 9000 is the best beard trimmer you can buy these days. If its $100 price tag is too steep, the baby-brother Multigroom 5000 is a solid fallback. It’s not shower-proof, has a shorter warranty (five years to the 9000’s eight years), has a plastic body instead of steel, and comes with a few less attachments. But at $40, it gets the basics done nearly as well as it’s pricier sibling.

Can you use a beard trimmer to cut head hair?

It has been revealed that beard trimmers are not meant to be used as hair clippers, since clippers require much more power to cut through thicker patches of hair. However, some beard trimmers have the muscle to multitask, and they’ll proudly hype that skill—usually by declaring the work for “beard and head” or similar language. We usually verify those claims against product reviews, too. And frankly, we’d probably just opt to buy a dedicated hair trimmer (you can find our roundup of the best hair trimmers here), especially if you’ll be using it often.

Which beard trimmer do barbers use?

Barbers choose tools to suit the job, from adjustable trimmers for controlling length, to detail trimmers for sharper edges. The Wahl Pro Series High Visibility is our professional pick for precision work, while the Philips Norelco Multigroom range offers broader versatility. For home use, start with your beard length and the kind of maintenance you do most often – a tool built for crisp outlines won’t necessarily include the guards you need to trim a longer beard evenly.

Which trimmer number is best for a beard?

Sources indicate that that's going to depend on what beard style you're going with. In order to play around with trimmer numbers, we like the Braun All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 9440 for its easy-to-use adjustment wheel.

How do you use a beard trimmer?

First, wash and dry your beard so you're starting off with a clean canvas. Then, decide how short or long you want to keep that bad boy. Trim against the grain of your growth, and know that the direction of growth may vary even in similar locations on the face. It's OK to make a couple of passes to ensure you get each hair because a patchy beard is a bad beard. Finally, clean up the neckline with some sharp lines so it's neat and tidy, framing the perfection that is your beautiful facial hair.

How do I maintain and clean a beard trimmer?

Recent findings suggest that switch it off and disconnect the charger before cleaning, then remove trapped hair from the blades and combs after each use. Follow the instructions for your particular model – a washable cutting head doesn’t mean the whole handle can go under the tap. The Remington Vacuum trimmer, for example, has removable washable parts, but its body should stay out of water.

Recent findings suggest that let washed components dry before putting them away. Oil the blades if the manufacturer tells you to, but don’t assume every trimmer needs it. Philips’ current Multigroom blades are designed to work without oiling. Replace a damaged or persistently blunt cutting unit with the correct part for your model.

How do I choose the right trimmer if I have sensitive skin or ingrown hairs?

According to recent reports, avoid “zero-gap” trimmers, which is a trimmer that cuts as close to the skin as possible, effectively a 0mm cutting length—those can mess your skin if you're prone to irritation or ingrowns. Otherwise, since you're trimming, you usually won't have to worry about irritating your skin because the blades shouldn't ever actually make contact with your face.

What’s the best way to travel with a beard trimmer—any TSA or voltage concerns?

According to recent reports, one of the big concerns for frequent travelers—at least in the USA—is whether they're going to be able to get their beard trimmer through security and not having it buzz during transport. If this is a priority for you, look for a model with a travel lock like the Braun All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 9440, which prevents the trimmer from turning on in transit.

How do I clean a waterproof vs. non-waterproof trimmer?

Waterproof trimmers are a breeze: Just hit ‘em with the (usually included) cleaning brush, then wash them off in the sink before drying and applying some oil. Non-waterproof trimmers just skip the rinse, so you’ll have to take extra care with the brush. You can also use spray cleaners specifically designed for grooming electricals depending on your trimmer's care instructions.

What should I do if my trimmer starts pulling hair or losing power?

According to recent reports, first, make sure you've thoroughly cleaned the trimmer. Next, make sure it's fully charged and/or has fresh batteries. If it's still pulling hair, it's probably time to swap the blades (plenty of companies sell refills on their site, and make sure to check the warranty to see if you qualify for a fresh set). If it's losing power, it might be time to swap the internal battery (check your warranty!) or get a new trimmer altogether. Luckily, we haven't had that concern with any of the trimmers listed above.

Where others zig, Whitney Peak zags.

The actor, who just wrapped the lengthy press tour for her new film, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, easily could have indulged in a method dressing spree (and many of her castmates did!). But it was Peak’s restraint that earned her a spot on Vogue’s 2026 Best Dressed list. “It’s my first time doing a press tour of this scale, and with all nerves and excitement, I just wanted to feel like myself in whatever I was wearing,” the actor tells Vogue.

“We talked about [method dressing], but ultimately decided not to,” she says of working with stylist Karla Welch. “I think the fun was in watching fans find their own connections between my character and what I was wearing.” Instead, Peak and Welch were guided by instinct. “I had a very general Pinterest board that I shared with Karla: images, textures, shapes I loved. But honestly, we worked very intuitively with each other and established a real flow,” she says. “The looks reflected that—they feel connected, have a rhythm, and they feel authentic.”.

Though she wore Chanel aplenty (“I had too much fun in that dress,” she says of her black multi-patterned look in Berlin), brands of all size were on the table. Peak was particularly enamored with the quilted floral silk jacquard Dries Van Noten coat she paired with a suit and tie (“THAT COAT! Everything.”) and the cutout Torishéju she trotted out in New York (“I’d never worn anything like it.”).

Recent findings suggest that and, although she swore off method dressing, Peak did end with an overt nod to her character, Lenore Dove Baird, in a blue velvet Robert Wun, a white dove pulling at her suspended shoulder strap. “The Robert Wun was the perfect, magical ending,” she notes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

According to recent reports, I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he remarked he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Recent findings suggest that take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

Mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

Set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

Transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

Sources indicate that place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very rapidly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

Recent findings suggest that bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

Do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

In anticipation of your next soirée, trade your go-to LBD for something a little more striking—Tove’s crushed-velvet maxi dress in stunning sapphire, to be exact. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, chances are you are reading this while awash in the joyful glow of an active oven and/or open laptop chock full of Black Friday sales. As someone who can’t help but enjoy America’s annual week of consumption, I have some advice: You can probably skip that fourth slice of pie and also, when it comes to gift-giving, bigger is not always better. Personally, some of the best presents I’ve received over the years are small but meaningful items that come with a sense of personal connection and discovery: A set of irresistible Japanese incense from an aspirational boutique my fiancé found in Tokyo’s Aoyama district. Some adorable silk painted ornaments that my mom stumbled upon at a local maker’s market. Employee merch from NASA, where my stepfather worked. All that to say, the ritual of gift-giving is always made to be much more meaningful when we can collect all the little, delightful items we’ve collected over the year and share them with those whom will appreciate them most. Maybe that’s a simple, but utterly practical thingamajig that has made your life that much more convenient. Or something you came across in your travels. Even an item you have at home for years that you couldn’t imagine living without. Here are a few self-care accessories that I've encountered both recently and not-so-recently that fit that bill.

Ever since the days of chewable Flintstones vitamins, we as a human race have been striving for new, inventive ways to get our daily dose in. Straight pills are boring and require water. Powders are messy and not easily transported. Gummies can be overly sugary and harden over time. But strips are nearly weightless, easy to travel with, and consumable on their own. The ones made by StripIt dissolve on your tongue, a little like a Listerine mint strip, and come in four different formulas: Vitamin C, D3 + K2, B12, Sleep, and Digest. Though they can take a little bit longer than a mint strip to dissolve, they’re still a really convenient way to make sure you’re keeping up with your supplements. I’ve been using the D3 + K2 ones while I travel. They taste pretty good and are colorful and novel enough to function as a small stocking stuffer or Hanukkah gift for the health hawk in your life.

Sources indicate that I will never tire of a big, beautiful block of soap. Especially if it's so fragrant that it fills a whole room with its smell. My latest favorite in this category is Life Research Lab, an herb-forward brand that takes inspiration from (and incorporates) the local LA flora into its soap blends. There’s the eucalyptus and grapefruit pumice slab that draws from common neighborhood trees, a classic “cowboy cologne” mix of cypress and California sagebrush so commonly found in Angelenos’ gardens, and a juniper bergamot number that lifts scents from the desert. Many of them contain bits and pieces of the very plants they’re named for, which function as light exfoliants as you scrub. I was especially charmed by the Christmas Morning Soap, which is infused with balsam fir essential oil and pinyon pine leaf. Its name, price, and the fact that it comes in both 9-ounce blocks and 4-ounce cylinders make it a perfect stocking stuffer. T’is the season.

Sources indicate that when I traveled to Seoul a few years ago, I popped into the Hinok store and spent about 20 minutes smelling basically every one of its products, which all contain ingredients sourced by foraging detritus from old cypress forests on Jeju island (not cutting them down). Alas, I couldn’t bring anything home because my carry-on was already stuffed. But recently I learned the brand is available to buy in the US and had a chance to try a few things out. My favorite is the thick, gooey body wash. It has the consistency of honey, and emanates a light, fresh natural scent without being too overpowering. Most crucially, the formula is gentle enough to clean your body without stripping it of its natural oils. After searching for a light body wash I can use daily for a while now, this qucikly became my fresh favorite. (The deodorising spray is really good for households with pets too.).

Recent findings suggest that when I was in Latest York last month, my future sister in-law suggested we take a quick field trip to Senti Senti, a little skincare store in Chinatown. To my delight, they carried imported Korean and Japanese formulas of lotions, cleansers, and—most importantly—sunscreen from popular brands like Beauty of Joseon and Bioré. (Don’t ask me how this is allowed, Chinatown’s gonna Chinatown.) In the 15 minutes we spent there, we observed at least three people walk in and beeline for this Dr. Althea face lotion and I couldn’t help but be tempted. Using it for the past month, I’ve been impressed with how light, hydrating, and easily absorbing it is—an excellent goop to apply in the morning. For anyone who hates the lingering feeling of a heavy day cream, this one’s a no-brainer.

In a recent development, we’re days away from the start of winter, meaning we’ll all be heating up our homes and braving, windy, sub-zero temperatures more regularly for the next few months. All of that means our skin has a far higher chance of getting dry and flaky. Enter Bein All-Over Body Oil. The blend of organic sesame seed, squalane, and camellia oil rubs on smoothly and absorbs like a dream, leaving no sticky residue behind. Body oil can be especially helpful for feet, knees, elbows, and hands, post-shower. And is light enough that you can apply lotion on afterward, too. Best of all, the San Diego-brand’s products smell faintly of bitter citrus, like a little Aperol spritz for your skin. It’s bright-red packaging makes it feel especially festive for the holidays.

A good robe, in my humble opinion, must rise to a few crucial tasks. It should be able to absorb water well, dry out swiftly, and let your skin breathe after a long warm soak in the bath or shower. It should also allow you to lounge around your household without flashing your living companions or getting furniture wet. That’s why I’m partial to a long linen kimono, which checks all of those boxes. I was gifted a sophisticated blue-striped one from Deiji Studios nearly six years ago for Christmas, and it’s now a perfectly worn-in, indispensable bathroom staple. No wonder Deiji still sells it. Even better, it’s on sale for Black Friday.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that “Lab-grown diamonds are the great equalizer,” says Jean Dousset, the great-grandson of Louis Cartier who pivoted his namesake label to exclusively lab-grown stones in 2023. “People don’t have to compromise anymore to own something exceptional.” Once considered the understudy to mined diamonds, these stones (and therefor, the best ​lab-grown diamond brands), have officially taken center stage—and they’re not just performing, they’re dazzling. Lab-grown diamonds are real diamonds. Not simulants, not stand-ins. We’re talking pure carbon, identical in chemical, physical, and optical makeup to what’s been pulled from the earth for centuries—just made in a lab, not dug up from a mine.

Industry observers note that so why the lingering hesitation? Stigma, mostly. The kind passed down like an heirloom from an era when “real” luxury was defined by scarcity and secrecy. But times—and tastes—have changed. “I started working with lab-grown diamonds because it was a smarter, more conscious choice,” states Jennifer Fisher, who now incorporates them across her fine jewelry designs. “They offer the same brilliance and clarity—but they align with how I want to shop and design today.” In an article that ran earlier this year, Jessica Sailer, former Vogue editor and founder of the new lab-grown line Pietro offered this: “Imagine if Hermès introduced an AI technology that could produce a perfect Birkin bag using the same materials in the same atelier, but in a fraction of the time. The craftsmanship would be identical. Would you want one?” Why, yes; yes, of course!

That sentiment is echoed by a growing number of designers (and their clients) who love that you can go bigger, bolder, and cleaner—ethically and aesthetically—without inflating the price tag.

In a recent development, of course, the Four Cs still matter—color, cut, clarity, and carat—but so do the other Cs: conscience, customization, and carbon footprint. Whether you're buying a diamond ring for a fiancée, a friend, or yourself (because yes, self-gifting is a love language), lab-grown diamonds offer a compelling—and undeniably glamorous—case for the future of fine jewelry. Ahead, discover the 11 best places to shop for lab-grown diamond jewelry, from dainty necklaces to diamond earrings to show-stopping statement pieces.

In the realm of fine jewelry, Kinn stands out as a purveyor of modern heirlooms designed to transcend fleeting trends. Founded in 2017 by Jennie Yoon, Kinn was born from a deeply personal mission: to recreate and reimagine her family’s stolen antique jewelry. This intimate origin story infuses each piece with a sense of continuity and timelessness, aiming to be cherished across generations.

Kinn’s collection seamlessly blends classic elegance with contemporary minimalism. From meticulously crafted engagement rings and wedding bands to everyday essentials like the Solis ring—a bestseller featuring an elegant ribbed design inspired by Yoon's mother’s vintage pleated ring—each piece embodies a narrative of heritage and modernity. Crafted in Los Angeles, the brand works with recycled gold and offers both lab-grown and natural diamonds.

According to recent reports, nearly a decade after launching the business, Yoon continues to build on the idea that a family heirloom needn't be inherited to have sentimental value. The result is jewelry that feels as though it might have belonged to your grandmother, while looking entirely at home in your own jewelry box.

Styles offered: Everyday fine jewelry, engagement rings, wedding bands, personalized and custom jewelryPrice range: Current prices vary.Special services: Personalized and custom designs, custom resizing, repairs, free shipping on orders $200+, returns offered within 10 days on domestic orders.

Not your mother’s Pandora. The Danish jewelry giant, once synonymous with charm bracelets, has undergone a rather chic reinvention. Consider its recent collaborators: makeup maestro Pat McGrath, who brought her signature glossy lips and mystical motifs to a collection of charms and rings, and Harry Lambert, the stylist behind Harry Styles’s most memorable looks, who gave the humble charm a baroque-pearl makeover. At Vogue World: Milano, Anok Yai even took to the runway in a bespoke Pandora necklace and earrings featuring a lab-grown diamond Mystic Eye charm. Quite the evolution from the charm bracelets of yesteryear.

The brand’s lab-grown diamond offerings, introduced in 2022, are similarly geared toward a upcoming generation of jewelry lovers, with tennis bracelets, delicate studs, and rings that make diamonds feel less like a once-in-a-lifetime purchase and more like an everyday indulgence.

Styles offered: Rings, earrings, necklaces, bracelets, and everyday fine jewelryPrice range: Lab-grown diamond pieces originally debuted from $290; current prices vary.Special services: IGI certification for qualifying diamonds, gift-ready packaging, and in-store shopping.

Brilliant Earth has long been at the forefront of ethically minded fine jewelry, and in the world of lab-grown diamonds, it was an early adopter. The brand first introduced lab-created stones in 2012—well before most retailers caught on—and has continued to push the category forward with collections that prioritize innovation and transparency. “We started Brilliant Earth to raise the ethical standards of the diamond industry and to create a new way to buy beautiful fine jewelry,” said co-founder and CEO Beth Gerstein in 2024.

In recent years, the brand has introduced collections like Capture, which features diamonds grown using captured carbon dioxide, and its Renewable collection, which emphasizes renewable energy in diamond production. A partnership with Dr. Jane Goodall also resulted in a limited-edition jewelry collection supporting conservation efforts.

According to recent reports, but perhaps the most glamorous development arrived in 2026, when Brilliant Earth joined forces with the House of Taylor for a collection inspired by Elizabeth Taylor's legendary jewelry box. The 17-piece assortment reimagines Old Hollywood extravagance with lab-grown diamonds and colored gemstones, drawing on the actress's famously expressive approach to jewelry. Think Taylor-level glamour, minus the Richard Burton-sized budget.

Alongside these more adventurous collections, Brilliant Earth continues to offer classic engagement rings, wedding bands, and everyday diamond jewelry, with an emphasis on customization and information about the origins of its stones.

Styles offered: Lab-grown diamond engagement rings, wedding jewelry, everyday fine jewelry, fancy-colored stones, custom designsPrice range: Pieces start at $225Special services: Free shipping, free 30-day returns, independent certification and grading reports, lifetime warranty, lifetime diamond upgrade program, flexible payment options, loose diamonds, custom designs.

Recent findings suggest that dorsey, the cult-favorite jewelry label founded by Meg Strachan at the end of 2019, has redefined heirloom jewelry for the modern era. Inspired by her grandmother's trove of vintage gems, Strachan released the direct-to-consumer brand with a mission to craft archival-inspired designs using lab-grown stones. Its signature Rivière necklaces and Georgian-inspired Lucien earrings have become recognizable favorites among a fashionable clientele.

According to recent reports, taylor Swift famously wore Dorsey earrings during her All Too Well short film, giving the brand a front-row seat to pop culture history. Hailey Bieber, Bella Hadid, and Emily Ratajkowski are also admirers, layering Dorsey's white sapphires and lab-grown diamonds with enviable ease.

Now, Strachan is expanding her jewelry vocabulary. In September 2026, Dorsey introduced earth-toned lab-grown diamonds, dramatic vintage-inspired drop earrings, and solitaire rings in seven different shapes. The collection is part of a broader exploration of colored stones and unexpected materials, from enamel to floating emeralds.

The effect is jewelry that looks more collected than coordinated—as though its wearer has spent years haunting antique shops, even if the pieces arrived in the mail last Tuesday.

Styles offered: Fine and fashion jewelryPrice range: $115 - $5,000Special services: Free two-day shipping, returns up to 30 days, limited-edition capsule drops.

It has been revealed that ​With a devoted celebrity following that includes Taylor Swift, Gigi Hadid, and Selena Gomez, Mejuri has firmly established itself as a go-to jewelry label for crafting irresistible, everyday pieces. Vogue’s Jewelry Director, Daisy Shaw-Ellis, encapsulates its appeal: “Its pieces are egalitarian and versatile—two things we value greatly.”​.

It has been revealed that building on its commitment to accessible luxury, Mejuri expanded into lab-grown diamonds in 2023, aiming to make high-quality diamonds more attainable without compromising sustainability. Co-founder Noura Sakkijha explains, “Our expansion into lab-grown diamonds is a way to make high-quality diamonds (especially the larger sized stones) more accessible to our customers, without compromising our sustainability efforts.” ​.

Industry observers note that the collection features timeless classics reimagined with lab-grown diamonds, including tennis bracelets, pavé rings, and simple pendant necklaces—ideal gifts for a loved one or oneself. More recently, Mejuri's 2026 Interconnected collection has taken inspiration from the handwritten “xo,” translating the familiar sign-off into looping, sculptural gold forms punctuated with lab-grown diamonds. It's a rather charming interpretation of love letters for a generation more accustomed to sending texts.

Styles offered: everyday fine jewelry, engagement rings, wedding bands in yellow gold and whitePrice range: Pieces start at $498Special services: 1:1 styling services in-store or virtually, free shipping on orders $75+, returns offered within 30 days.

Long before buying an engagement ring online felt second nature, Blue Nile was helping convince a generation of shoppers to take the leap. Founded in 1999, the tech giant was among the first to bring the traditionally intimidating business of diamond shopping to the internet, allowing customers to compare stones, customize settings, and find their dream ring without ever setting foot in a jewelry store.

Industry observers note that in 2026, Blue Nile welcomed another pioneer of online diamond shopping into the fold: James Allen, whose standalone website closed in May. Known for its pioneering 360-degree diamond imagery, James Allen made it possible to scrutinize a potential stone from virtually every angle. Its designs now live on as a proprietary collection at Blue Nile, bringing together two of the original names in digital diamond retail.

Recent findings suggest that today, Blue Nile offers everything from classic solitaires and wedding bands to tennis bracelets and diamond studs, with both natural and select lab-grown diamonds available. For the bride-to-be who knows exactly what she wants—or the one who'd rather explore a thousand possibilities before deciding—there's something rather appealing about having the jewelry counter at your fingertips.

Styles offered: Engagement rings, wedding bands, loose diamonds, earrings, bracelets, and fine jewelryPrice range: Varies by stone and settingSpecial services: Customizable engagement rings, online diamond selection, 360-degree diamond imagery for eligible stones, and virtual consultations.

Recent findings suggest that for the diamond maximalist looking to dabble in lab-grown, Grown Brilliance is for you. The brand works exclusively with lab-grown diamonds—no mined options—and it indicates in the scale, sparkle, and scope of its offering. Whether you're designing your dream engagement ring from scratch or shopping one of the label's ready-to-ship bestsellers (hello, bezel-set pendant necklaces and brilliant-cut studs), the emphasis here is on choice.

According to recent reports, founded by third-generation jeweler Akshie Jhaveri, Grown Brilliance has lately been looking backward for inspiration. Its September 2026 Heirloom collection borrows from Georgian-era jewelry, incorporating rose cuts, collet settings, and intricate metalwork into a 42-piece assortment. Then came Stella, a celestial collection inspired by the painted constellations on the ceiling of New York's Grand Central Terminal. Proof that even the most technologically advanced diamonds can have a wonderfully old-fashioned sensibility.

For shoppers with something more specific in mind, the brand's Design Your Ring program allows customers to choose a diamond and setting, with grading reports available for eligible stones. It's a modern approach to fine jewelry that leaves plenty of room for personal expression.

Styles offered: Engagement rings, wedding jewelry, everyday fine jewelry, custom designsPrice range: Pieces start at $125Special services: Free shipping and returns, lifetime warranty, certification cards, loose diamonds, Design Your Ring program.

According to recent reports, jean Dousset may be the great-grandson of Louis Cartier, but his career has never been about resting on pedigree. With early training at Chaumet in Paris and an apprenticeship under Alain Boucheron, he rapidly established himself in the world of high jewelry, eventually working at Van Cleef & Arpels. But it was when he opened his own showroom in Los Angeles that Dousset began rewriting the rules on his own terms.

In April 2023, he made perhaps his boldest move yet: transitioning his entire brand to lab-grown diamonds. The pivot wasn't just about ethics—it was about creative freedom. “The fact that it's cheaper doesn't make it cheap,” Dousset told Vogue. Fine jewelry, after all, still requires imagination, creativity, design, and craftsmanship, whatever the origins of the stones.

In a recent development, that creative license is on full display in Dousset's recent work, including the bespoke engagement ring he designed for Paris Jackson, featuring a portrait-cut diamond and distinctive sculptural metalwork. Rather than simply recreating a conventional engagement ring, the design reflects Jackson's own aesthetic and personal symbolism.

Recent findings suggest that today, Dousset's lab-grown diamonds appear in designs that reflect both his Place Vendôme roots and a thoroughly modern sensibility. It's jewelry that honors tradition—while giving it a long-overdue update.

Styles offered: Engagement rings, wedding jewelry, everyday fine jewelry, custom designsPrice range: Pieces start at $1,200Special services: GIA-certified stones, custom designs, complimentary consultations, free shipping, 14-day returns.

Industry observers note that think you know Kendra Scott? Think again. The designer best known for her kaleidoscopic gemstones and bold silhouettes has taken a chic detour into the world of lab-grown diamonds—and the result is decidedly more minimalist. Her fine jewelry expansion, introduced in 2024, marked a noticeable shift: refined bands, delicate drop earrings, and whisper-thin pendants crafted with diamonds and pared-back elegance.

It has been revealed that more recently, the Kendra Scott Collection has taken the designer's diamond offerings in a slightly tougher direction, with sculptural spike necklaces, personalized charms, and architectural silhouettes. It's a far cry from the colorful statement earrings that first made Scott a household name—and an intriguing glimpse of the brand's grown-up era.

The collection still speaks to the Kendra Scott customer—approachable, warm, and sparkle-loving—but with a sleeker edge. For those accustomed to her signature drusy stones and vibrant hues, the diamond edit offers something subtler: a timeless, everyday kind of luxury that doesn't need to shout.

Styles offered: Necklaces, earrings, bracelets, rings, and watchesPrice range: Pieces start at $25, with fine jewelry options reaching up to $8,995Special services: Customizable jewelry through the Color Bar experience; lab-grown diamonds graded at or above H color and VS clarity, with stones 0.5 carat or higher certified by the International Gemological Institute.

Jennifer Fisher has always approached jewelry as deeply personal—and deeply powerful. The designer, known for redefining modern essentials with her signature hoops and dog tags, entered the lab-grown diamond space not to jump on a trend, but to offer something meaningful. “I have a mine-cut stone that is of significant size,” she told Vogue, “and I don’t know who, if anyone, was harmed mining it. That doesn’t feel great.”.

According to recent reports, her lab-grown collection, released in early 2023, is a sharp departure from the micro pavé-drenched engagement offerings flooding the market. Think pinky rings with major emerald cuts, simplified martini-set studs, and substantial tennis necklaces made to sit perfectly whether your hair is up or down. "I stopped wearing my engagement ring on my wedding finger three years ago,” Fisher explains. “Now I wear it on my pinky—and people literally stop me on the street.".

Recent findings suggest that designed in 18k gold, her pieces favor substantial, single-stone silhouettes over sparkle overload. “The market is already saturated with pavé,” she notes. “People want one visually extraordinary stone—not a bunch of tiny ones shoved into a setting.”.

Though she doesn't initiative to expand into traditional engagement rings, Fisher has found that women—particularly those buying for themselves—are gravitating toward her lab-grown pieces as milestone markers: for anniversaries, divorces, or just the joy of wearing a serious rock on any finger they please. “They’re not buying them to be subtle,” she says. “They’re buying them because they want a stone that feels bold, modern, and truly theirs.”.

Styles offered: Rings, tennis necklaces, diamond studsPrice range: Pieces start around $3,000Special services: Simple, signature settings; lab diamonds set in 18k gold; direct-to-consumer model with personal consultation.

According to recent reports, think of Rare Carat as your diamond-savvy best friend—only armed with AI, GIA gemologists, and access to over a million diamonds. Introduced in 2016 as a search engine for comparing diamond prices (“Kayak for diamonds,” as it was dubbed early on), the platform has since evolved into one of the most trusted managed marketplaces in the lab-grown diamond space.

Industry observers note that the brand’s lab-grown offerings lean into value and transparency without sacrificing quality. Their expansive inventory includes diamonds of every cut, carat, and clarity imaginable—many available with 360° HD imaging and grading reports from trusted labs like IGI and GIA. Every customer is paired with expert concierge support (yes, even via text), making it easy for first-time shoppers to navigate the process with confidence.

In November 2026, Rare Carat added more than 70,000 fancy-colored lab-grown diamonds to its inventory, including pink, blue, and yellow stones. For anyone who has ever admired a spectacular colored diamond at auction, it's an intriguing opportunity to experiment with some rather extraordinary hues without the extraordinary auction-house estimates.

It has been revealed that what sets Rare Carat apart? Its tech-forward model. “We’re using AI to analyze diamonds, predict value, and detect overpricing,” says founder Ajay Anand. Whether you’re shopping for a classic solitaire or a custom engagement ring with a personal twist, Rare Carat offers a data-driven path to diamonds—no jargon, no pressure.

Styles offered: Customization options for engagement rings, wedding bands, loose diamondsPrice range: Lab-grown diamonds start around $500Special services: AI-powered diamond value scoring, 360° HD imaging, free gemologist checks, 30-day returns, custom ring builder.

To help guide your shopping journey, we tapped four jewelry experts to answer the most frequently asked questions about lab-grown diamonds. From the science behind the sparkle to their ethical implications, consider this your lab-grown cheat sheet.

A Brief History of Lab-Grown Diamonds.

Industry observers note that lab-grown diamonds aren’t newly introduced, per se. The technology has been around for decades – General Electric produced the first batch in 1954 – but early versions were largely industrial-grade, used for cutting tools, not rings. Only in the last decade has quality and accessibility caught up with demand. “The technology around lab-grown diamonds had been going on for a long time,” states Jean Dousset, “but had not reached the quality that it did a few years back.”.

By the time the Gemological Institute of America (GIA) began grading lab-grown diamonds using the same scale as natural diamonds, Dousset knew the tide was turning: “That was a big breakthrough. The foremost authority in diamond grading acknowledging that these are two diamonds that are the same – with a different origin – meant the product was viable.”.

Industry observers note that what is a lab-grown diamond? Are lab-grown diamonds real diamonds?

According to recent reports, “Lab-grown diamonds are molecularly exactly the same as mined diamonds. In 2018, the FTC updated their definition of what a diamond is, reflecting that lab-grown diamonds are indeed ‘real’ diamonds,” states Strachan. “The only difference between a lab-grown diamond and a mined diamond is the setting in which it’s created – under heat and pressure in a controlled lab setting versus under heat and pressure in the earth.”.

How are lab-grown diamonds made?

Recent findings suggest that lab-grown diamonds undergo the same formation process, just at warp speed in a lab. There are two primary methods to forming lab-created diamonds:.

High Pressure High Temperature (HPHT): Mimics Earth’s natural diamond formation process using a small diamond seed, subjected to over 1.5 million pounds per square inch of pressure and temperatures above 2,000°F.

Industry observers note that chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD): Places a diamond seed into a vacuum chamber filled with carbon-rich gas. The gas is heated until the carbon atoms crystallize on the seed, layer by layer.

"The ability to create diamonds in the lab means growers can control for the desired color, cut, clarity, and size,” says Strachan.

However, it’s worth noting that the process requires significant energy input. According to the Natural Diamond Council, CVD methods can consume 250-750 kWh of electricity per carat – comparable to running an average U.S. household for a month. The energy footprint varies widely depending on the lab’s source (renewable vs. fossil fuel).

How can you tell the difference between the best lab-grown diamonds and natural diamonds?

With the naked eye, “it’s nearly impossible to tell the difference between mined and lab-grown diamonds,” indicates Strachan. “Only a gemologist with the most trained eye is able to tell the difference, and even this is presently under scrutiny,” she adds. “I hear from many Dorsey customers that they layer a Dorsey lab-grown necklace next to a mined diamond necklace, and no one can tell the difference.”.

What is the highest grade of lab-grown diamonds?

Lab-grown diamonds can reach the highest grades of Flawless (FL) or Internally Flawless (IF) clarity, D color, and Super Ideal Cut. However, achieving these top grades remains rare.

“Although lab diamond technology has advanced tremendously, the highest color and clarity grades, such as D/FL and D/IF, are still difficult to achieve,” says Annie Chen, Brilliant Earth’s senior vice president of merchandising.

Do the 4 Cs apply to lab-grown diamonds?

In a recent development, absolutely. Cut, color, clarity, and carat weight remain essential considerations when buying a lab-grown diamond, just as they are for a mined stone. What has changed is how certain laboratories communicate those qualities. In October 2025, the Gemological Institute of America introduced a new assessment system for eligible lab-grown diamonds, classifying them as either Premium or Standard rather than using its traditional natural-diamond grading nomenclature. Other laboratories, including IGI, continue to provide detailed grading reports using the familiar 4 Cs. In either case, it's worth looking beyond carat weight alone: a beautifully cut diamond can be far more captivating than a larger stone with less sparkle.

Do lab-grown diamonds hold their value?

Industry observers note that there’s no simple answer here. “Value,” as Fisher puts it, “isn’t always about resale.” The jewelry market still treats mined diamonds as rarer, and thus more valuable, but as Dousset points out, “Just because something costs less doesn’t mean it’s cheap. It’s about access – being able to buy the ring you actually want.”.

Are lab-grown diamonds more ethical?

In a recent development, “Symbolically, the fact that we’re not digging into the ground to unearth diamonds resonates,” states Dousset. While lab diamonds still require significant energy, some labs operate entirely on renewable power and produce zero emissions.

The better question may be: what’s the overall impact of a company’s operations? “It comes down to traceability,” notes Chen. “That’s where the ethics lie.”.

#135816. The 20 Most Iconic Colognes of All Time, According to GQ in 2026

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (3015 w)
