📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the humble oat is having something of a wellness renaissance.
  • Dubbed “nature’s Ozempic” on social media right now, oats are enjoying a surge in popularity as interest in GLP-1 medications influences how we shop and eat.
  • “I eat oatmeal every day,” says dermatologist and nutritionist Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the humble oat is having something of a wellness renaissance. And while oatmeal may not be the most glamorous of breakfast foods, it’s definitely one of the healthiest. There’s a reason, after all, that oats have been eaten for thousands of years.

Dubbed “nature’s Ozempic” on social media right now, oats are enjoying a surge in popularity as interest in GLP-1 medications influences how we shop and eat. According to a latest report from British supermarket Waitrose, as reported by The Guardian, sales of its Scottish oats have increased by 124% this year. There’s also the rise of so-called “fiber math”—the practice of incorporating more fiber into everyday meals through additions like chia seeds, nuts, and berries. And while no food can replicate the effects of prescription GLP-1 medications, oats are naturally rich in beta-glucan, a soluble fiber that supports gut health and helps us feel fuller for longer. Consider it a newfound appreciation for an age-old breakfast staple.

“I eat oatmeal every day,” says dermatologist and nutritionist Dr. Christian Merkel of the Skin and Laser Center in Munich, Germany. “For me, they are a real superfood—and totally underrated.” He notes that not only is oatmeal good for digestion—a key factor in overall health—but it also provides long-lasting feelings of satiety. Below, six reasons why oatmeal should be a regular star in your morning line-up.

“Oatmeal contains a large amount of fiber, which makes it very good for healthy digestion,” indicates Merkel. Oats contain both soluble and insoluble fiber: The former, most notably beta-glucan, absorbs water to form a gel-like substance in the digestive tract, while the latter helps add bulk to stools and promotes regular bowel movements. A half cup of dry rolled oats provides around four grams of fiber—a good head start on your recommended daily intake. To further boost the fiber content of your breakfast, try adding ground flaxseeds, chia seeds, raspberries, or chopped almonds. And remember to drink plenty of water throughout the day to help all that fiber do its job.

According to recent reports, oatmeal is a good source of vitamin K, which is essential for bone health and blood clotting. It also contains B vitamins—especially B1 (thiamine) and B5 (pantothenic acid)—which are essential for converting protein, carbohydrates, and fats into energy, supporting the digestive tract, making red blood cells, producing hormones, and for healthy skin and eyes.

“Studies have shown that oatmeal has been proven to lower cholesterol levels and can therefore also be beneficial against cardiovascular disease,” says Melker, noting that this is also thanks to beta-glucan, the soluble fiber in oats.

Oatmeal contains essential minerals such as copper, zinc, calcium, and potassium. It’s also rich in magnesium—important for energy, sleep, muscles, protein formation, the nervous system, genes, and more—and is especially high in the inflammation-reducing trace mineral manganese.

Oats are a great plant-based source of protein. “If you compare the nutritional values of different types of grains, you will find that the values of oatmeal are excellent,” says Merkel, noting that this helps balance out the carbohydrates. “The protein content is very good at 5.3 grams per half cup.”.

According to recent reports, though some glucose-experts disagree, Merkel says oatmeal is a safe option for those wishing to keep their blood sugar in check. “There is virtually no sugar in oatmeal which means that your insulin level will not rise quickly when you eat oatmeal,” he says. “Instead, there is a very slight, healthy rise in blood sugar and therefore long-lasting satiety.” Additionally, oats have been shown to lower blood sugar levels—especially in people with obesity or who have type 2 diabetes—thanks to good ol’ beta-glucan’s ability to slow the emptying of the stomach.

Recent findings suggest that the existing story already covers fiber, vitamins, heart health, minerals, protein, and blood sugar. I’d add two points on antioxidants and the gut microbiome, expanding on the latter in a way that distinguishes it from the existing fiber section.

It has been revealed that oats have something of an edge over other grains when it comes to antioxidants. They contain a distinctive group of naturally occurring plant compounds called avenanthramides, which researchers have identified as having antioxidant and potential anti-inflammatory properties. While more research is needed to understand their effects on human health, they offer another reason to appreciate the nutritional complexity of the humble oat. For an extra hit of antioxidants at breakfast, top your oatmeal with blueberries, raspberries, or a sprinkling of cinnamon.

Industry observers note that your morning bowl of oatmeal is also breakfast for the beneficial bacteria in your gut. The fiber in oats acts as a prebiotic, feeding gut bacteria that, in turn, produce compounds called short-chain fatty acids. These play an important role in maintaining the intestinal barrier and supporting immune function. A study published in 2026 in Nature Communications also explored how interactions between oats and the gut microbiome may contribute to their cholesterol-lowering effects. To make your morning oatmeal even more gut-friendly, try adding a spoonful of live-culture yogurt or kefir for a combination of prebiotics and probiotics.

Industry observers note that be sure to choose steel-cut whole oats instead of instant oats, which have less fiber and nutrients. Choose organic if possible. And, “bear in mind that a large proportion of the vitamins and trace elements are broken down during the cooking process,” indicates Merkel, who adds that the healthiest way to eat oats is actually “uncooked.” If that sounds a little too rustic for you, he recommends the two alternatives below:.

To make the overnight oats, place oats in a small bowl and pour in a plant-based drink of your choice until the oats are completely covered. “Personally, I’m a big fan of unsweetened almond milk because it has the best nutritional value of all plant-based drinks and the taste also appeals to most people,” states Merkel, who recommends enhancing the oats with nutritionally-rich spices such as cinnamon and turmeric. “Turmeric is rich in antioxidants and just a teaspoon is enough to make breakfast even healthier,” he says. Cover the oats and leave them to soak in the refrigerator for eight to twelve hours. “In the morning, you can add another superfood in the form of blueberries. Dark berries are also rich in antioxidants,” suggests Merkel. “If you prepare your oatmeal in this way, you have a super healthy breakfast that is rich in fiber and antioxidants and, unlike packaged muesli, only gently raises your insulin levels and keeps you full for a long time.”.

Sources indicate that merkel notes oats can be easily added to your usual protein shake or smoothie for a boost of extra protein, nutrients, and fiber. “Add one to two tablespoons of uncooked rolled oats and some fresh fruit into the blender. The oats give the shake a pleasantly nutty taste and the vitamins are retained during the blending process,” he says.

Preheat oven to medium broil and line a medium baking sheet with aluminum foil. In a medium bowl, toss onion with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Add flour and Panko and toss until the onions are coated. Broil, tossing every 2 to 3 minutes, until onions are crisp and golden, about 6 to 8 minutes total. Turn oven down to 375°.

Prepare an ice bath. In a large pot of heavily salted boiling water, add green beans and cook until bright green, 3 to 4 minutes. Using a slotted spoon or tongs, quickly transfer green beans to the ice bath to cool. Drain and transfer to a large bowl.

In a large skillet over medium heat, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil. Add shallots and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 5 minutes. Add mushrooms and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring often, until mushrooms are golden, about 5 minutes more. Stir in garlic, then transfer the mixture to the bowl with the green beans.

In a recent development, heat the remaining 4 tablespoons of olive oil in the same skillet over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook until golden, about 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in almond milk and bring to a simmer.

Sources indicate that cook until thickened, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and season to taste with salt and pepper.

Add the green bean mixture and toss until everything is evenly combined.

In a recent development, transfer the mixture to a medium casserole dish. Bake until warmed through and bubbling around the edges, about 20 minutes. Top with the "fried" onions and bake for 5 minutes more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, where does one even begin when narrowing down the best perfumes for women? It’s a daunting task, to say the least. With hundreds of thousands of women’s fragrances flooding the market (and that’s putting it mildly), finding your signature scent or building out a fragrance wardrobe can swiftly lead to sensory overload.

First, there’s the matter of personality and preference: Everyone’s idea of “the best” is deeply personal and sometimes even polarizing. Are you drawn to hyper-femme blooms, or do you lean toward moody, spice-forward aromas? What about delicious gourmands, warm solar scents, or—conversely—earthy notes grounded in fresh greens and wood? Perhaps you are a no-fuss minimalist who sticks to subtle skin scents. Are you interested in something long-lasting or a light and airy eau de toilette? Maybe you’d rather layer a few different perfumes to create your own unique combination. The choices are quite literally endless.

Whether you prefer standout blends from legacy houses or niche scents from innovative alchemists—there’s something for everyone, with picks from experts and Vogue editors alike. Ahead, our definitive guide to the best perfumes for women, along with expert tips on finding the perfect scent that feels uniquely yours. Prepare for a sensory journey that balances tradition and innovation.

According to recent reports, if we haven’t driven the point home already: Fragrance is deeply personal. So what’s the secret to finding the best fragrances? Look no further than your reflection. “The most important thing to consider when looking for a signature fragrance is choosing one that reflects who you are as a person,” says fragrance expert Nwasike, reminding us that scent should be an extension of self—intimate, expressive, and unmistakably you.

On a more practical note? It’s all about testing, testing, and yes—more testing. Start by spritzing your top contenders on fragrance blotter strips. Once something sparks that visceral “yes,” only then should you see how it plays with your skin. This step is key, notes Nwasike, to “understand the true nature of the fragrance” and how it will evolve with your body chemistry throughout the day.

In a recent development, not one for snap decisions? No problem. Nwasike recommends trying samples or gift sets before committing to a full bottle. Consider it your scent’s trial period—a little like dating before marrying a signature scent.

For those just beginning their fragrance journey, one of the first questions that often arises is: What’s the difference between eau de toilette and eau de parfum? The distinction lies in concentration—and, ultimately, longevity. “Eau de parfum (or EDP for short) generally contains between 15% and 20% fragrance oil,” explains fragrance expert Levy. As a result, it tends to last around four to five hours on the skin.

Eau de toilette, on the other hand, is lighter and more fleeting. “The term comes from the French phrase faire sa toilette, meaning ‘to get ready,’” indicates Levy. Designed for a quick, refreshing burst of scent, eau de toilette typically lingers for two to three hours and contains between 5% and 15% fragrance oil.

Sources indicate that craving serious staying power, maximum projection, and a swoon-worthy scent trail? Pick an extrait or absolut perfume—the most concentrated forms of fragrance. “Every perfumer works differently, so there is no single method for creating an extrait,” perfumer Aurélien Guichard of French label Matière Première previously told Vogue. What you can expect, though, is intensity, richness, and a scent that truly lingers.

How to Make Perfume Last Longer.

Making sure your fragrance lasts with you throughout the day is more than just a spritz-and-go experience. “To extend the longevity of a fragrance, your skin needs to be hydrated,” says Nwasike, who opts for applying a rich mositruizer before spraying her perfume. For more of a boost, you can even mix in a perfume oil with your body moisturizer for added layering. And while we’re spraying, don’t just opt for skin contact. “Always spray your fragrance on your clothing, because fragrance on fabric slows the evaporation process," says Nwasike.

According to recent reports, last but certainly not least, where you store your fragrance matters just as much as how you wear it. Nwasike advises storing your perfume in a cool, dark, and dry place, as direct sunlight can break down fragrance molecules.

In a recent development, in curating this edit, we considered the elements that make a fragrance truly unforgettable. First and foremost: captivating notes designed to turn heads. Our selection spans iconic blends from storied fragrance houses to fresh, modern offerings from emerging perfumers shaking up the scene. Yes, there are the universally adored staples—Carolina Herrera Good Girl, Marc Jacobs Daisy, Viktor & Rolf Flowerbomb, Versace Bright Crystal, Gucci Bloom, and Miss Dior. All icons no doubt. But our goal? To guide you toward something a little less expected—something not already dominating your TikTok FYP.

With insights from industry experts and Vogue editors alike—who shared the scents that draw the most compliments—we’ve crafted a tightly edited list that celebrates the art of standing out subtly.

Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 325°. Toast ½ cup raw walnuts on a rimmed baking sheet, tossing halfway through, until golden brown, 10–12 minutes.

Meanwhile, cook 2 bunches collard greens, ribs and stems removed, leaves cut into 2" pieces, in a large pot of generously salted boiling water until just tender, 9–11 minutes. Using tongs, immediately transfer to a large bowl of ice water and let cool.

Whisk 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, ¼ cup white wine vinegar, 2 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, preferably country-style, ⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil, ¼ cup (packed) coarsely chopped tarragon, 2 tsp. sugar, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl to combine. Set dressing aside.

In a recent development, transfer toasted walnuts to a small bowl and drizzle with remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Sprinkle with a generous pinch each of sugar and salt and toss to coat. Taste and add more sugar if needed (nuts should be more sweet than salty). Set seasoned walnuts aside.

Sources indicate that drain collard greens and squeeze gently to remove excess water. Transfer to bowl with reserved dressing and toss to coat evenly. Cover and chill at least 15 minutes and up to 2 hours.

Recent findings suggest that arrange greens in a shallow bowl or on a platter and spoon any dressing remaining in bowl over. Top with seasoned walnuts and tarragon leaves.

Do Ahead: Walnuts can be toasted and dressing can be made 1 day ahead. Store walnuts airtight at room temperature. Cover dressing and chill.

Sources indicate that sen. Chris Van Hollen revealed Thursday night that he would run for Senate majority leader, launching a challenge to Sen. Charles E. Schumer of Newly introduced York, the current Democratic leader.

Industry observers note that van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat first elected to the Senate in 2016, served in leadership in the House and has been chairman of both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. He has remarked since the midterm elections he was listening to fellow Senate Democrats about the possibility of a run for the top job.

According to recent reports, “In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen stated in a statement. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need fresh leadership. This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”.

Sources indicate that “I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the vital work ahead. Schumer's supporters were quick to highlight the success at the ballot box in 2026, with the Democratic caucus potentially growing to 56 seats if former Rep. Mary Peltola prevails in Alaska.

According to recent reports, in keeping with the World Series theme, Sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., echoed King with her own statement of support for Schumer.

“The Brewers just had a record season, and next year is not the time to change our management," Baldwin said. "The same is true in the Senate.”.

In an interview with MS NOW about his run, Van Hollen conceded that Schumer would be the favorite in the secret-ballot contest, which will take place in December.

“Am I the underdog? Yes,” Van Hollen said. “You’re talking about an incumbent who uses the power of incumbency to, you know, provide deals to people.”.

Van Hollen outlined legislative priorities including restoring Medicaid funding that Republicans cut in last year's budget reconciliation law and extending Affordable Care Act tax credits. But he suggested Democrats need to go further.

Industry observers note that "We need to extend tax credits for the Affordable Care Act, but we can’t stop there, right? We have a completely broken health care system. It’s become profits, not people. And so my view is, we also need in the first 100 days to make health care more affordable for tens of millions of people," Van Hollen remarked. "We need to immediately make it clear that nobody’s going to pay one penny to subsidize data centers. ... We need to make sure that we have a livable minimum wage.".

He also said he would not take sides in contested Democratic primaries, and he would make sure the DSCC did not take money from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC.

It has been revealed that van Hollen's early backers include progressive Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who emerged from a hotly contested Democratic primary in Michigan while the Senate Democratic political apparatus was backing Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich.

Industry observers note that “In April, I was the first candidate in the country to call on Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats, and I am proud to stand with him in his bid to become Senate Majority Leader,” El-Sayed said in a statement. “Michiganders demand money out of politics, money in pockets, and Medicare for All. Sen. Chris Van Hollen offers both the courage to go toe-to-toe with the Trump administration to deliver for working people and the experience to maneuver the Senate caucus. It’s why he has my full support to lead our caucus.”.

Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

According to recent reports, meghan Markle may have traded the sunny climes of Montecito for the British countryside, but her penchant for a thoughtful tablescape, a homemade preserve, and a well-appointed guest room remains. As the Duchess of Sussex prepares to celebrate her first Thanksgiving since relocating to the UK, she’s imparting some of her festive hosting wisdom.

In the forthcoming winter issue of Bon Appétit, Meghan shares her approach to holiday entertaining, alongside conversations spanning family, favorite restaurants, and the duchess’s Netflix series, With Love, Meghan.

Sources indicate that long before she had her own lifestyle brand (or, indeed, her own wine), Meghan was a college student looking to impress her dinner guests with a little help from Rachael Ray. An avid viewer of 30 Minute Meals, she recalls making a rather sophisticated grilled cheese sandwich in her first apartment, layering fontina, apple slices, and thyme, pressing it all together on her George Foreman grill, and finishing it with olive oil and Maldon sea salt. The wine pairing was Trader Joe’s famously inexpensive Two Buck Chuck. “Early 2000s at its finest,” she recalls.

It has been revealed that while Meghan’s taste in wine has evolved somewhat (last summer saw the launch of her own Napa Valley rosé), her approach to entertaining hasn’t changed all that much. “I still believe little touches are all you need to make something ordinary feel special, especially when you're having loved ones over,” she tells the magazine. “It doesn't have to be over the top.”.

So, what does a stay at the Sussexes’ entail? She likes to lay the table a day in advance, freeing herself up to actually enjoy the company of her guests when they arrive. For those staying overnight, she programs the coffee machine to brew before they wake up, stocks the kitchen with breakfast provisions (think bagels, berries, yogurt, smoked salmon, and capers), and leaves a handwritten note inviting them to help themselves.

It has been revealed that and when Meghan is the guest rather than the hostess? She favors something edible and homemade, like a batch of honey-roasted spiced nuts or a blackberry pound cake that can double as breakfast the following morning. Presentation is part of the pleasure too, and she advises using a little kitchen twine, a length of ribbon, or a sprig of rosemary to make things feel more considered. (Both recipes feature in the fresh issue.).

According to recent reports, those who tuned into last year’s festive instalment of With Love, Meghan will be familiar with the duchess’s enthusiasm for the holidays. The Netflix special saw her making personalized advent calendars for her children, decorating her Christmas tree with slices of fig, and preparing cacio e pepe gougères with restaurateur Will Guidara. Her companion lifestyle brand, As Ever, has leaned further into the art of gifting, too. Earlier this fall, Meghan marked the launch of its latest holiday collection with a sweet video of her five-year-old daughter, Princess Lilibet, helping her make raspberry jam.

This year’s festivities will look a little different for the Sussexes. Having relocated to England in late August after six years in California, Meghan Markle and Prince Harry are celebrating Thanksgiving on British soil for the first time since 2018—and for the first time in the UK with both Archie and Lilibet. Recent weeks have afforded us some glimpses into their new life in England, from a family outing to a holiday fair to Meghan’s reunion with her longtime London-based hairstylist and friend George Northwood.

The duchess’s home may have changed, but her brand of Montecito mom domesticity remains intact.
